hook: A 1972 Brutalist school campus built as McAteer High School, now the Ruth Asawa San Francisco School of the Arts.

historic_status.reason: No evaluation and 45 years or older

building.name: Ruth Asawa San Francisco School of the Arts

historic_survey.survey: Modern & Postmodern Architectural Styles Historic Context Statement (2024)

historical_record.description: McAteer High School enrolled 1,700 students on this campus, against a stated capacity of 2,569.
The School of the Arts was established here as part of McAteer High School, and taught on the campus for ten years.
The School of the Arts became a separate high school, ending its first ten years on this campus; by December 1997 it was housed in a surplus elementary school on Font Street.
J. Eugene McAteer High School closed.

The School of the Arts was again housed in buildings on this campus. A district plan to move it to 135 Van Ness Avenue had completed environmental review but was unfunded, and no relocation was planned in the near term.
The Academy — San Francisco @ McAteer opened here as a second high school on the campus.
The Academy — San Francisco @ McAteer closed, leaving the School of the Arts as the only school recorded at this address.

unknowns: The assessor's roll classes the parcel as a vacant lot in public use and records no year built; Planning's Modern and Postmodern context statement dates the building to 1972.
The state's school directory gives McAteer High School an opening date of 1 July 1980, and the school was already enrolling students at this address in 1974.
